ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vьdova, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *widewāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁widʰéwh₂. Cognate with English widow, German Witwe, French veuve, Spanish viuda, Italian vedova, Sanskrit विधवा (vidhavā).

s.g: to cause (a horse, etc.) to rear up
to cause (hair, etc.) to stand on end
cry, wail, howl, yell, scream (prolonged cry of distress or anguish)
x: Стыд, страх, скорбь, жа́жда раска́яния, жа́жда вели́кого де́йствия, мгнове́нного по́двига — всё разреши́лось э́тою ме́дленною, неудержи́мою до бо́ли, до су́дороги в челюстя́х, бо́лее стра́шною, чем вопль и рыда́ние, безнадё́жною зево́тою.

s.g: to set in, to be established
it is unfortunate, it is regrettable, unfortunately, regrettably

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic истина (istina), from Proto-Slavic *jьstina, from *jistъ. Compare Latvian īstens (“real, true, genuine”).

s.g: calibre (diameter of the bore of a firearm)
checklist (list of things to be verified)

ety.text: Borrowed from Japanese 漫画家(まんがか) (mangaka).

s.g: abbreviation of мно́жественное число́ (mnóžestvennoje čisló, “plural number”)

to stuff (with), to pack (with), to fill (with)

ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *obixodъ. By surface analysis, оби- (obi-) + ход (xod).

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic прѣпона (prěpona), from Proto-Slavic *perpona. Cognate with пина́ть (pinátʹ, “to kick”).

s.g: to burst open, to cause to burst
to overflow, to fill up, to fill to the brim, to be brimming over (with), to swell (with), to bloat (with)
